label: thm:counterintro
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:counterintro}
There exist a graphic matroid $M_1$ and a partition matroid $M_2$ on the same ground set such that $\chi(M_1,M_2)=2$ and $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)=3$.
head: environment

label: cla:k4
title: Proof
head: environment

label: cla:k4
title: Claim
body_md:
\label{cla:k4}
Two complementary $3$-edge sets of $K_4$ are both spanning trees if and only if exactly one pair of opposite edges is split between them.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If an opposite pair is contained in one part, then cardinality forces another opposite pair to be contained in the other part and the third pair to be split. Both parts are then connected and have three edges, hence are spanning trees. Conversely, suppose that no opposite pair is contained in either part. Then all three opposite pairs are split. A set obtained by choosing one edge from each opposite pair of $K_4$ is either a triangle or a star, and its complement is respectively a star or a triangle. Thus the two sets cannot both be spanning trees.

label: prop:reduction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:reduction}
Let $M=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be a strongly base-orderable matroid, and suppose that $E=I\cup J$ for two disjoint independent sets $I$ and $J$. Then $M$ has a reduction to a unit-capacity partition matroid whose classes have size at most two.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Extend $I$ to a basis $B_1=I\cup C$ with $C\subseteq J$, and extend $J$ to a basis $B_2=J\cup A$ with $A\subseteq I$. Then $B_1\cap B_2=A\cup C$, $B_1\setminus B_2=I\setminus A$, and $B_2\setminus B_1=J\setminus C$.

Apply strong base orderability in the contraction $M/(A\cup C)$ to the disjoint bases $I\setminus A$ and $J\setminus C$. There is a bijection $\varphi\colon I\setminus A\to J\setminus C$ such that $((I\setminus A)\setminus X)\cup\varphi(X)$ is a basis of $M/(A\cup C)$ for every $X\subseteq I\setminus A$. Let $N$ be the unit-capacity partition matroid whose classes are the pairs $\{x,\varphi(x)\}$ for $x\in I\setminus A$, together with the singletons $\{e\}$ for $e\in A\cup C$.

To see that $N$ is a reduction of $M$, let $T$ be independent in $N$, and let $X$ be the set of those $x\in I\setminus A$ for which $\varphi(x)\in T$. Then $T\subseteq ((I\setminus A)\setminus X)\cup\varphi(X)\cup A\cup C$. The first two terms form a basis of $M/(A\cup C)$, while $A\cup C$ is independent in $M$, so the set on the right is a basis of $M$. Hence $T$ is independent in $M$.
head: environment

label: cor:sbo
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:sbo}
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be strongly base-orderable matroids on a common ground set. If $\chi(M_1)\le2$ and $\chi(M_2)\le2$, then $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)\le2$. In particular, if $\chi(M_1,M_2)=2$, then $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)=2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Applying \cref{prop:reduction} to each matroid gives unit-capacity partition matroids $N_1$ and $N_2$ such that every $N_j$-independent set is $M_j$-independent and every partition class of $N_j$ has size at most two. The common independent sets of $N_1$ and $N_2$ are the matchings of a bipartite multigraph of maximum degree at most two. By Galvin's theorem~\cite{galvin1995list}, this multigraph has a proper list edge-coloring from arbitrary lists of size two. The resulting color classes are independent in both $M_1$ and $M_2$, so $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)\le2$. The equivalent formulation follows from the theorem of Davies and McDiarmid mentioned in \cref{sec:preliminaries}.
head: environment

label: qu:gap
title: Question
body_md:
\label{qu:gap}
Is there a constant $C$ such that $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)\le \chi(M_1,M_2)+C$ for every pair of matroids $M_1,M_2$? In particular, does $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)\le \chi(M_1,M_2)+1$ always hold?

label: qu:sbo
title: Question
body_md:
\label{qu:sbo}
Does $\chi_\ell(M_1,M_2)=\chi(M_1,M_2)$ hold whenever $M_1$ and $M_2$ are strongly base-orderable?
